chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said, 'Can the fasting one chew the gum?' He said: 'No'.
ai.seo_question: Does chewing gum break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that chewing *ews* (a type of resinous gum) invalidates the fast, establishing a precedent for substances that are consumed or absorbed through the mouth. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it extends the prohibition of eating and drinking to include the mastication of consumable substances, emphasizing the preservation of the fast's spiritual and physical integrity. The brevity of the report highlights the Imam's direct application of general principles to specific daily practices.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I said, ‘The Fasting-one, can he chew the gum?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who chews chewing gum when fasting.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’”
